study type: Retrospective cohort study with a prospective observational component
exposure: Letrozole (LE) combined with human menopausal gonadotropin (HMG) endometrial preparation protocol for frozen embryo transfer
Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) with GnRH-a pretreatment endometrial preparation protocol for frozen embryo transfer
outcome: Vaginal microbiota profiles (Lactobacillus, Gardnerella, Escherichia-Shigella, Staphylococcus abundance)
cohort: The study included women with endometriosis undergoing frozen embryo transfer, with 770 FET cycles analyzed in the retrospective cohort and 105 women participating in the prospective vaginal microbiota analysis.
finding: The LE + HMG regimen, despite comparable live birth outcomes, was associated with fewer obstetric complications (fewer cesarean deliveries and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy) and a more favorable vaginal microbiota profile compared to the GnRH-a HRT protocol.
mod_finding: The LE + HMG group showed significantly fewer cesarean deliveries (64.9% vs. 75.4%, P = 0.020) compared to the GnRH-a HRT group.
